title: The Secret to Perfect Masala Dosa 🔥 #shorts
dish_fact: The dosa's signature tang and lightness come from wild fermentation - the rice-and-urad-dal batter is left overnight so natural lactic bacteria leaven it, no yeast and no baking soda.

segments.moment_description: A covered clay vessel of dosa batter resting overnight on a rustic wooden shelf in dim, warm village-kitchen light, the batter risen and gently bubbled at the surface to imply long fermentation, Studio Ghibli style

The young woman in a white-and-gold sari drops mustard seeds into shimmering hot ghee in a black kadai; the seeds crackle and pop, then a handful of fresh curry leaves is dropped in and splutters, extreme close-up, steam rising, warm morning light

A ladle of pale dosa batter poured onto a screaming-hot flat tawa and immediately spread outward in one smooth spiral with the base of the ladle, the surface bubbling and the lacy edges already crisping and lifting, steam rising, top-down close-up

Golden spiced potato masala spooned in a line along the centre of the crisp dosa, then the dosa folded over the filling with a flat wooden spatula, ghee glistening on the crackly golden surface, close-up
The finished folded dosa lifted off the tawa with both hands and set down onto a fresh green banana leaf, its shattering-crisp edges catching the warm light, a thin curl of steam rising

Overhead hero shot of the plated masala dosa on a banana leaf with a small bowl of coconut chutney and a bowl of steaming sambar, garnished with fresh coriander, rich and appetising, soft morning light, Studio Ghibli style
